name: Jennie Si
title: Professor; School of Life Sciences Interdisciplinary Graduate Faculty
department: School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering
fitReason: Strong direct learning-control fit: develops and executes online actor-critic adaptation for physical wearable robots, including personalization without a human-motion simulator.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete 27-page ICML 2025 AIP paper initializes an online actor-critic from behavior cloning of one person’s unassisted walking. It then adjusts pneumatic soft-exosuit inflation onset/duration for five healthy adults walking on a level treadmill at 1m/s. Raspberry Pi/solenoid hardware, IMU/EMG sensing and offline Vicon measurements are specified. Policy updates occur per five-step gait sample, not every sensor tick. Pressure/timing bounds and model-conditional analysis support the tested setup, not a general human-safety guarantee. Outcomes concern gait and EMG effort; clinical rehabilitation and impaired-user benefit are explicitly future. The ASU commencement record identifies lead author Junmin Zhong’s 2025 PhD under Si, and May 2026 ASU technology-transfer material independently connects Si to this continuing exosuit technology. Hardware remains a joint ASU project; no exclusive lab access is assumed.
